description: The Jan 20 Bamako gathering is described as “dozens/several dozen” in opened event reports. Those reports demand the departure of French forces but do not establish a demand directed at Mali’s own government or policy.
required_followup: Review opened contemporaneous organizer statements and independent attendance reporting for an exact crowd of at least 50 and an explicit domestic state-policy target.

description: Meguetan Infos and Bamada search results describe a Jan 28 Mali Tè Kila meeting/front against implementation of the Algiers agreement, but the underlying pages were unavailable to this worker and full event context remains unverified.
required_followup: Read the original articles if accessible and record their date, origin, publicness, attendance, demands, and any state response.

description: This is an open-web first pass with French- and English-language searches; no Bambara or other local-language queries were completed, Lexis-Nexis/all-news access was unavailable, and coverage across regions and sectors remains uneven.
required_followup: Continue weekly, regional, and sector-specific review using local-language and newspaper-archive sources where available; do not infer that no other events occurred.

description: A later UNTM-government agreement search result mentions negotiations during January and 149 HUICOMA workers who had observed a sit-in at the Bourse du Travail, but it does not date that sit-in. The 149 workers are not a verified crowd estimate.
required_followup: Recover the sit-in chronology and determine whether a January public gathering occurred; keep the number of workers distinct from people physically assembled.

description: The Jan 28 Mali Tè Kila lead may be an organizational or “patriotic meeting” rather than a public protest. Search excerpts do not verify an open gathering, actual attendance, or crowd size.
required_followup: Establish whether a public action actually took place and whether at least 50 people assembled before deciding protest eligibility.

description: The Jan 21 Bamako caravan is corroborated by opened HIIK and Maliweb reporting, but the worker-side source for tear-gas dispersal and the claim of no arrests is a search-only Bamada excerpt; other response fields remain unknown.
required_followup: Check the full local report and attribute each response claim separately; retain unknown values for arrests, beatings, shootings, deaths, accommodation, or ignore unless directly evidenced.

description: Several search results describe the Jan 27 FORC-G march in Gao and its demands; the worker-side reports remain search-only. A “thousands” estimate comes from the same publisher as other Gao reports and is not independently confirmed.
required_followup: Inspect original local reports, determine source origin and attendance basis, and preserve the distinction between the reported march and prior-year killings mentioned as a demand.

description: A Bamada article schedules a CDR/M5-RFP caravan for Jan 22, while another archive result may indicate a separate executed caravan. It is unresolved whether a Jan 22 action occurred or whether the later report refers to Jan 21.
required_followup: Recover the linked Jan 22 report and distinguish any actual follow-up action from the Jan 21 caravan before adding or merging a candidate.

description: CEN-SNESUP sources describe a strike beginning Jan 5 with an intended Jan 5–9 duration; an opened Jan 13 report says the strike call was lifted Jan 7. Exact work-stoppage coverage and dates remain uncertain, and no public gathering is documented.
required_followup: Clarify the strike’s realized duration and whether any distinct public assembly occurred; do not treat the work stoppage alone as a protest gathering.
